summary: Mid-cycle downgrade caused prorate rounding gap and microburst invoice charge
description: Issue summary: Customer downgraded reserved capacity mid-billing-cycle. After the downgrade, they observed an unexpected microburst line on the next provisional invoice and a small negative credit missing from the hourly prorate reconciliation. Impact: Customer reports a $1,320 microburst charge that they believe should have been offset by a prorated reserved credit. This is blocking autopay and causing finance escalation. Environment: Dedicated reservation on prod (us-east) with hourly metering enabled; customer has hybrid reserved/hosted fallback enabled. Relevant timeline: 2026-03-03 downgrade request processed at 08:13 UTC, billing window cut at 09:00 UTC, provisional invoice generated 2026-03-04 02:12 UTC. Expected behavior: After downgrade, reserved-hours prorate should reduce the reserved charge and apply a matching hourly credit to host/microburst usage; rounding should not create a net unexplained charge. Observed behavior: A microburst line item billed at reserved-rate appeared, and the prorated reserved credit applied was 1 cent less than the microburst offset, leaving the $1,320 charge. Customer supplied screenshots of provisional invoice and screenshots of reservation dashboard. They also attached CSV of hourly postbacks for the 24-hour window across the downgrade.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer requests a downgrade of reserved capacity during an active billing hour (example: 2026-03-03 08:13 UTC)
Billing system closes hourly window at top of hour (09:00 UTC) and generates postbacks for that hour
Proration job calculates reserved credit across partial hours and applies rounding rules to cents-level line items
Microburst usage from hosted fallback is billed at the host rate and intended to be offset by reserved prorate credits
Generate provisional invoice and compare per-line rounding totals
logs: Postback summary (2026-03-03 08:00-09:00 UTC): reserved_hours_consumed=42.5, host_microburst_tokens=1,200,000, reserved_rate_usd_per_hour=0.25, host_rate_effective=0.30
Proration job run id: prorate-2026-03-03-09:01:12, rounding_policy=round-half-to-even, calculated_reserved_credit= -1320.00, applied_credit=-1319.99
Invoice generator trace: invoice-run-2026-03-04-02:12, invoice-delta-log shows residual 0.01 USD not applied to line item 2431-microburst-hosted
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage and ticket creation. Attached provisional invoice PDF and hourly postback CSV. Requested urgent review from Billing team.
Liam O'Connor (Billing Eng): Assigned for investigation. Noted that proration uses cent-level rounding after summing micro-buckets. Asked for raw postback ingestion timestamps.

Customer (Acme Analytics - finance contact Sarah Patel): Confirms downgrade time and attached their internal billing screenshot. Requests hold on autopay until confirmed. Asks for expected refund timeline.
Priya Desai (SRE): Flagged potential race between reservation state change and hourly postback aggregator; suggested replaying postback window to validate determinism.
Liam O'Connor (Billing Eng): Requested temporary waiver of autopay hold and submitted provisional credit if root cause identified.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Rounding policy (round-half-to-even) applied after aggregation of per-subsecond microbatches causes 1 cent delta when cross-hour prorate intersects with microburst rounding.

Hypothesis 2: Reservation downgrade processed but reservation metadata (effective_timestamp) saved with microsecond truncation, causing postback aggregator to include a ~47s slice of reserved-hours at old rate.

Checked postback ingestion logs for 08:00-09:00 UTC window; found 12 postbacks with timestamps between 08:59:15 and 09:00:02 UTC. Two postbacks were ingested after the downgrade event was processed, but before the aggregator cut-off, leading to mixed-rate attribution.

Replayed aggregator for that hour in staging with identical postbacks: observed same 0.01 USD delta when using round-half-to-even; switching to round-up eliminated residual but changes global rounding semantics.
Cross-reference: SUP-25788 (reserved-capacity invoice generated mid-cycle) shows similar timing edge-cases; recommend evaluating the aggregator boundary handling in both tickets.

Temporary regression found in release billing-service v2.14.1: a change to decimal normalization introduced microsecond truncation in effective_timestamp stored in reservation table. Rollback to v2.14.0 avoided the delta in staging replay.
resolution: Workaround: Applied provisional 0.01 USD credit to Acme Analytics account to offset rounding gap and held autopay for this invoice cycle. Long-term fix: Backed out decimal normalization change from billing-service (rolled to v2.14.0) in prod on 2026-03-11 01:45 UTC; added extra logic in postback aggregator to enforce cut-off strictly before effective_timestamp and to aggregate using fixed-point cents arithmetic before rounding. Follow-ups: create a GA task to add integration test covering reservation state transitions during hourly cutover (linked to INT-4423), and run a retro to decide preferred rounding policy across microbatch aggregation. Finance notification: Issued provisional credit and confirmation email to customer (Sarah Patel).
